To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(1) The structure of Lumbricus hemoglobin has been determined to be a 12-subunit tetramer with a 2-fold axis of symmetry, and (2) The structure of the molecule is similar to that of the hemoglobins of other annelids.

the three-dimensional structure of Lumbricus hemoglobin has been determined by electron microscopic tomography and that the molecule has a hollow central core and an open structure with large gaps between adjacent 1/3 subunits.
(i) the structure of the hemoglobin was determined by STEM; (ii) the structure was reconstructed from the STEM data; and (iii) the reconstruction was consistent with X-ray projections of the model.
In summary, our research is concerned with

the development of new techniques for obtaining three-dimensional reconstructions of macromolecules from electron micrographs and with the application of these techniques to the study of hemoglobin and other biological systems.
the development of new algorithms for three-dimensional reconstruction of macromolecules from a small number of electron micrographs.
the development of methods of image processing for electron microscopy and their application to the analysis of biological macromolecules.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the reconstruction represents an approximate three-dimensional model of the molecule.
the reconstruction of a biological molecule from a small number of projections is feasible.
the three-dimensional reconstruction of the hemoglobin molecule is consistent with the X-ray diffraction data and with the model proposed by Perutz and his colleagues.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

the three-dimensional reconstruction of the Lumbricus terrestricts hemoglobin from STEM computer-averaged images has been achieved with the use of a new method for the calculation of the two-dimensional sections of the molecule from a restricted number projections.
the three-dimensional reconstruction of macromolecules by STEM is possible and that the technique has potential for the study of biological macromolecules.
, in the case of the hemoglobin, the three-dimensional reconstruction from four STEM projections is not as good as that from 30 electron micrographs.
The main takeaway from our work is that
STEM can be used to obtain a three-dimensional reconstruction of an object with an atomic resolution.
the STEM technique is an extremely powerful tool in the study of biological molecules, and the results are comparable to those obtained from x-ray crystallography.
it is possible to obtain three-dimensional information on a macromolecular assembly from a limited number of projections.
